title: On Sea Charts Formerly Used in the Marshall Islands, with Notices on the Navigation of These Islanders in General
version: English translation printed in 1901 in the Smithsonian Institution's annual report for 1899, pp. 487–508 and plates. Printed p. 487 credits the 1898 Marine-Rundschau original (pp. 1418–1439) and identifies added plates.
lineage: Original English-edition scan read, separate from Gulick's report. Scanned volume SHA-256 4b56a0514ed4962388657fdd54a10fbc4664494bdc7c08b0186a305f631813bd. Winkler reports accounts elicited and interpreted via local speakers during the colonial period. His early hearsay and later interpretation are distinguished on pp. 487–488.

passages.note: Winkler reports acquiring two specimens at Jaluit in July 1896, and learning more on a return visit in November 1897 from Lojak, with Laumanuan's explanations conveyed by Joachim de Brun.

passages.locator: pp. 494–496, chart classes and Chart I
passages.quote: only for general instruction without referring to any particular islands
passages.note: Separates mattang from rebbelib and meddo and illustrates how one mattang represented wave patterns between hypothetical islands. On p. 495, Winkler describes the use of charts as reminders and to teach navigational signs.
